_comment_seeded: IDENTICAL to fs_clean.json apart from input_path and output_file, and it
must stay that way: the two documents are the same statements, and any
difference between the two tables has to come from the DOCUMENTS, never
from two configs that drifted. The seeded document's three planted
defects all sit in the data (two wrong subtotals and one wrong note
reference), so none of them touches a label this config anchors on.
_comment_statements: The statements this document is expected to hold, in printed order.
Keys are the heading VERBATIM - note the em dash (U+2014) in the note
headings, not a hyphen. A mismatch fails the load rather than landing
rows under a heading nobody expected.
`sections` / `subsections` are DERIVED - the pages do not print them
consistently. The balance sheet prints 'Equity and liabilities' as a
header row but never prints 'Assets' or 'Equity' at all, and the income
statement prints no group headers whatsoever; its groups are inferable
only backwards, from a trailing subtotal. Declaring the ranges by label
keeps that inference in a file a reviewer can hold against the printed
page, instead of inside a heuristic. Every anchor is checked to resolve
exactly once.
`top_level` forces a line out of the hierarchy: Total assets sums
across both subsections of the assets half rather than belonging to
either.
`column_labels` overrides the printed header. Notes 5, 7 and 10 print
'SAR million' over their single value column and inherit the period of
the face statement they support - 31 Mar 2026 for the position note,
Q1 2026 for the flow notes. Note 9 is left alone: its three columns are
a breakdown axis, not a period.
